The Johto Isles — 16 Leaders

Walkthrough — how to get there. The Johto Isles are the very last post-game content: they sit behind the Elite Four rematch, and you sail to them from the Sevii Islands. If the ferry Sailor says the isles are closed, you haven't cleared that rematch yet.

1 · Unlock the ferry

  1. Beat the Elite Four and become Champion.
  2. Re-beat all eight Kanto Gym Leaders — their rematches open once you're Champion (Giovanni now stays in the Viridian Gym).
  3. That reopens the Elite Four; beat the rematch ladder through to the Champion. Winning it is what opens the ferry.

2 · Catch the boat

  1. Go to One Island in the Sevii Islands — reached by the Seagallop ferry from Vermilion City Harbor, the same one from the main story.
  2. In One Island Harbor (the dock hall where the Seagallop lands), talk to the Sailor on the pier. After the E4 rematch he offers passage.
  3. Say yes and he sails you to Skyreach Isle (Falkner).

3 · Island-hop all eight

  1. Each isle has two Leaders — a Johto Leader at the far end and a Hoenn co-leader. Beat both, then talk to that isle's Sailor to sail onward.
  2. Order: Skyreach → Chitin → Meadowmoo → Hollow → Ironfist → Foundry → Glacier → Wyrmspire.
  3. Beating Clair & Flannery on Wyrmspire (the 8th) clears the Johto circuit — which promotes the Kanto gyms to their Tier 3 rematch.

Rematches

All eight Kanto Gym Leaders — Giovanni included, who now stays in his gym instead of dissolving it and fleeing — plus the Elite Four and the Champion can be rematched, but only as a gated ladder:

  1. Clear the Elite Four to open the Kanto gym rematches (ace Lv 70), each with the mixed-generation Tier 2 roster.
  2. Re-beat all eight leaders to reopen the Elite Four as a Lv 78→82 ladder (Lorelei 78, Bruno 79, Agatha 80, Lance 81, Champion 82). Beating them a second time unlocks the Johto Isles.
  3. During the Johto phase, Kanto rematches let you choose the Kanto-only (Tier 1) or mixed (Tier 2) team — optional, non-gating.
  4. Clear all sixteen Johto leaders and the Kanto gyms jump to Tier 3 (ace Lv 92); re-beat all eight again to face the Tier 3 Elite Four (Lorelei 96→Champion Lv 100) — the hardest content in the game.

Find a Pokémon

Type a Pokémon's name to see every wild spot it appears — method, odds, and levels. (Wild encounters only; gift/evolution-only species won't list a spot.)

Find an item

Type an item's name to see everywhere it turns up — picked up in the field, hidden, given by an NPC, or sold at a mart. Poké Balls, TMs, berries, key items, all of it.

Locations

Every map in the game — its layout, the Pokémon you can find there (per method, with odds and levels), and the items waiting to be picked up or uncovered. Trainers and items are drawn onto each layout using their actual in-game overworld sprites:

Trainer — shown as their overworld spriteItem — a Poké Ball on the groundHidden item — a grayed-out Poké Ball (search here)

Open a map, then hover a trainer, item, or wild Pokémon to light up where it is — or click it to keep it highlighted and see its details (team, item effect, Pokédex peek). Click again to clear.

ItemsAntidoteAntidote. A spray-type medicine. It heals one POKéMON from a poisoning.AwakeningAwakening. A spray-type medicine. It awakens a sleeping POKéMON.Burn HealBurn Heal. A spray-type medicine. It heals one POKéMON of a burn.Ice HealIce Heal. A spray-type medicine. It defrosts a frozen POKéMON.Paralyze HealParalyze Heal. A spray-type medicine. It heals one POKéMON from paralysis.ReviveRevive. A medicine that revives a fainted POKéMON, restoring HP by half the maximum amount.Super PotionSuper Potion. A spray-type wound medicine. It restores the HP of one POKéMON by 50 points.Super RepelSuper Repel. Prevents weak wild POKéMON from appearing for 200 steps.
Poké BallsGreat BallGreat Ball. A good, quality BALL that offers a higher POKéMON catch rate than a standard POKé BALL.
TMs & HMsTM05 RoarTM05 Roar. A savage roar that causes the foe to switch out of battle. In the wild, ROAR ends the battle.TM15 Hyper BeamTM15 Hyper Beam. A harsh attack that inflicts severe damage on the foe. However, the user must rest the next turn.TM28 DigTM28 Dig. A 2-turn attack in which the user digs underground, then strikes. It can be used to exit dungeons.TM31 Brick BreakTM31 Brick Break. Strikes the foe with a rock-hard fist, etc. It shatters barriers such as REFLECT and LIGHT SCREEN.TM43 Secret PowerTM43 Secret Power. An attack move that may have an additional effect depending on the battle terrain.TM45 AttractTM45 Attract. The foe, if it is the opposite gender as the user, becomes infatuated and may not attack.

Evolutions

No trades needed. Trade evolutions now happen by level, or by using the item from the bag like a stone. Every item is sold at the Celadon Dept. Store, 4th floor. Cross-gen evolutions (Crobat, Blissey, Espeon, Umbreon and more) work from day one.

What's Changed

Everything this hack changes from vanilla FireRed, in one place. For the exhaustive stat-by-stat side-by-side vs. Yellow Legacy, see ChangeDoc.html.

  • Ghost is special, Dark is physical — the Gen 3 category fix.
  • Trade evolutions removed — Kadabra/Haunter evolve by level; Metal Coat, King's Rock, Dragon Scale & co. are used from the bag.
  • Weather buffs — hail 1.5× Ice Def, sandstorm 1.5× Rock Sp.Def; Magma Armor shrugs off Water.
  • Two modes — Normal and Hard (badge level caps that continue through the postgame rematch ladder: 70 → 82 → 88 → 92, then uncapped for the final League).
  • All 386 obtainable on one cartridge; every trade-locked mon reachable.
  • Built-in randomizer — chosen at New Game after the difficulty prompt. Wild Pokémon, route trainers, bosses, gifts & starter, and legendary statics each have their own switch, plus similar-strength matching and a legendary-pool option. The seed lives in the save file (shown on your Trainer Card), so a save always replays the same shuffle.
  • Hard Mode postgame caps follow the rematch ladder — 70 for the Kanto gym rematches, 82 for the Elite Four rematch, 88 through the Johto Isles, 92 for the Tier 3 gyms, then uncapped for the final League.
  • HMs are freely forgettable and TMs are reusable — no more one-shot TMs or HM-locked move slots, matching the other Legacy games.
  • Hard Mode permadeath — a fainted Pokémon is dead for good. It can't be revived or healed at a Center; swap in a living box mon to carry on.
  • Cut trees stay cut forever and never grow back; the pointless cut trees cluttering Fuchsia City are gone entirely.
  • Fuchsia PC/Gym reachable from the right side too — a new hedge doorway saves the long walk around the top (Yellow Legacy parity).
  • Celadon Dept. Store evolution counter now stocks every evolution item — the four elemental stones plus Sun/Moon stones and the old trade-evo items.
  • Rival's start tidied — he no longer lifts a Poké Ball off Oak's table before Oak hands him his Eevee.
  • Three Island bikers field distinct gang teams instead of three identical squads.
  • Aces beside every leader — each Kanto gym leader, the Elite Four, and the Champion now stand next to their ace Pokémon in the overworld (Onix by Brock, Gengar by Agatha, Dragonite by Lance…), using open-source Gen-3 overworld sprites.
  • Order-based gym scaling — Erika, Koga, Sabrina and Blaine can be taken in any order, and each leader fields a team scaled to your badge count (Lv ~35 → ~53), so they stay a real fight whenever you show up. Yellow Legacy parity.
  • Starters in the wild — Route 21 North's grass now yields Bulbasaur, Squirtle, Charmander and Eevee (Mr. Mime kept). A FireRed Reforged twist on Yellow Legacy: raise the classic starter line you didn't pick. (Try the Find a Pokémon search above.)
